lessons.title: Be a Guest at a Home Dinner
lessons.objective: ask what gift to bring, how to arrive, and what table manners are expected
lessons.focus: Apporter is a standard verb for bringing a gift to someone's home: j'apporte des fleurs; apporte une bouteille de vin. Amener often refers to bringing a person, while emporter means taking something away. Les hôtes means hosts in this scene; l'hôte can also mean a guest, and l'hôtesse is a woman host. Attendre que takes the subjunctive: attends que mes parents commencent à manger; attendre takes a direct object without a preposition: attendre ses parents. À quelle heure dois-je arriver ? uses polite, slightly formal inversion; in conversation with a friend, À quelle heure je dois arriver ? is also heard. Les bonnes manières is plural; les couverts usually appears in the plural when it means silverware. Keep a napkin sur les genoux. Arriver avec quinze minutes de retard, c'est normal is Lucía's statement about her family, not a general rule. The after-dinner conversation is rendered as discuter à table après le repas. Ne pars pas juste après le dessert is the negative imperative of partir. Si ça ne te dérange pas, est-ce que je peux aider ? offers help to Lucía.
lessons.scene: In Puebla, Mark is going to have dinner at the home of his friend Lucía's parents. He asks Lucía what gift he can bring, and she says that if he wants, a bottle of wine or a dessert is good, because her mom loves sweets. He asks what time to arrive, and Lucía says dinner is at 8, but in her family arriving 15 minutes late is normal. He asks whether there is anything he shouldn't do at the table. She explains her family's manners: wait for her parents to start eating, keep the napkin on the lap, and don't leave right after dessert, because her parents enjoy the after-dinner conversation. Mark buys a dessert at a pastry shop and some flowers for the hosts, and arrives with his gift ready.

cards.fr: Qu'est-ce que je peux apporter comme cadeau ?
Y a-t-il quelque chose que je ne dois pas faire à table ?
cards.en: Is there anything I shouldn't do at the table?

cards.fr: Vaut-il mieux apporter du vin ou un dessert ?
cards.en: Is it better to bring wine or a dessert?

cards.fr: Dois-je attendre que tout le monde commence à manger ?
cards.en: Should I wait for everyone to start eating?

cards.fr: Si ça ne te dérange pas, est-ce que je peux aider ?
cards.en: If it's not too much trouble, can I help with anything?

cards.fr: Dans ma famille, arriver avec quinze minutes de retard, c'est normal.
cards.en: In my family, arriving 15 minutes late is normal.

cards.fr: Attends que mes parents commencent à manger.
cards.en: Wait for my parents to start eating.

cards.fr: Garde ta serviette sur tes genoux.
cards.en: Keep your napkin on your lap.

cards.fr: Ne pars pas juste après le dessert.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Ce soir, Mark va dîner chez les parents de son amie Lucía, à Puebla.
reader.en: Tonight Mark is going to have dinner at the home of his friend Lucía's parents in Puebla.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: D'abord, il lui demande : « Qu'est-ce que je peux apporter comme cadeau ? »
reader.en: First he asks her: What gift can I bring?

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Lucía répond : « Si tu veux, apporte une bouteille de vin ou un dessert, parce que ma mère adore les sucreries. »
reader.en: Lucía answers: If you want, bring a bottle of wine or a dessert, because my mom loves sweets.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Mark veut aussi savoir : « À quelle heure dois-je arriver ? »
reader.en: Mark also wants to know: What time should I arrive?

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Lucía lui dit : « Le dîner est à vingt heures, mais dans ma famille, arriver avec quinze minutes de retard, c'est normal. »
reader.en: Lucía tells him: Dinner is at 8, but in my family arriving 15 minutes late is normal.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Puis Mark demande : « Y a-t-il quelque chose que je ne dois pas faire à table ? »
reader.en: Then Mark asks: Is there anything I shouldn't do at the table?

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Lucía explique les bonnes manières de sa famille : « Attends que mes parents commencent à manger et garde ta serviette sur tes genoux. »
reader.en: Lucía explains her family's manners: Wait for my parents to start eating and keep your napkin on your lap.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Lucía ajoute : « Mes parents aiment bien discuter à table après le repas, alors ne pars pas juste après le dessert. »
reader.en: Also, my parents enjoy the after-dinner conversation, so don't leave right after dessert.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.fr: Mark sourit, achète un dessert dans une pâtisserie et des fleurs pour les hôtes, puis arrive, son cadeau à la main.
reader.en: Mark smiles, buys a dessert at a pastry shop and some flowers for the hosts, and arrives with his gift ready.

lessons.internalReviewNote: Owner-only source-pinned draft. All 16 source English word meanings remain the first 16 cards in order; all nine Reader English lines remain exact. The 15-minute lateness belongs to Lucía's family and is not a general Puebla or Mexican norm. Requested Haiku 5.5 CLI returned Sonnet 5.5 metadata; Opus 5.5 read-only critique informed corrections to quotation attribution, tu/vous consistency, offering help, and overstatements in the focus. Qualified French review open: les hôtes is ambiguous with guests; French rendering of sobremesa; inversion register between friends; vingt heures vs huit heures du soir; ma mère vs maman; whether the help offer should address Lucía or her parents. No qualified approval.
